newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Vice President Joseph Estrada yesterday resigned as chairman of the Presidential Anti-Crime Commission, breaking ties with President Ramos in preparation for a run for the presidency next year. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- President Ramos yesterday ordered the police to go after a drug ring believed responsible for the killing of journalist Danny Hernandez. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- Faced with a formidable foe, the country's four major political parties have finally agreed to merge and field a common candidate for president in 1998. (TIMES/INQUIRER)

- The government will formally request the International Monetary Fund to extend the country's three-year economic programme after Congress said it will not be able to pass the tax reform package within the month, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said yesterday. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- SBC Warburg Securities will cooperate with regulatory agencies in the investigation of alleged dummy accounts in Sapphire Securities Inc involving three of its former and current analysts. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- San Miguel Corp and Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd of Australia announced yesterday they have entered into definitive agreements to integrate their operations in the soft drink business through a stock swap valued at about $2.7 billion. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
